events.title: GCC first public release
events.summary: Richard Stallman released the first public GCC on March 22, 1987 — a beta (0.9) C compiler that could bootstrap itself; GCC 1.0 followed around May 1987.
events.about: GCC compiled C (and later C++, Fortran, Ada, and more) for m68k, VAX, and other machines from a single codebase. Its retargetable backend and free license made Unix ports possible without proprietary compilers. Linux, GNU tools, and decades of open-source software were built with GCC before LLVM/Clang offered an alternative.

narrative.whyChosen: GCC was the flagship compiler of the GNU project and free software movement.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved a community-maintained, multi-platform compiler could match vendor toolchains.
narrative.problemSolved: Proprietary Unix compilers were expensive and tied developers to single vendors and architectures.
